::: {#exm-perplexity-uniform}
#### Perplexity of a uniform distribution

<!-- no-figure: the example is a single number -->

If $X$ is uniform on $k$ [values](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-realization),
then every value
has [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $1/k$
and [rarity](#def-rarity) $k$,
so by @thm-perplexity-geometric-mean the [perplexity](#def-perplexity) of $X$ is $k$.
In general, the perplexity is the count of equally likely values
that would give the same [entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy) as $X$.

:::
